facts.t: The phrase belongs to a Victorian historian of Greece
facts.d: George Grote coined it while writing about Athenian democracy. Ambedkar quoted him in the Constituent Assembly, warning that constitutional morality is not a natural sentiment — it has to be cultivated, because India's soil was still undemocratic.

facts.t: One doctrine overturned a judgment in nine years
facts.d: Naz Foundation struck down Section 377 in 2009 on constitutional morality; Koushal restored it in 2013; Navtej Singh Johar struck it down again in 2018 on the same reasoning. The doctrine lost, then won.

The Court placed constitutional morality above popular sentiment and permitted women's entry. The verdict met organised resistance on the ground and a review reference — the clearest case of a principle winning in law and stalling in practice.

bank.q: The term constitutional morality was coined by:
bank.e: George Grote, the British historian of Greece. Ambedkar imported the concept into Indian constitutional discourse during the Constituent Assembly Debates.

bank.q: With reference to constitutional morality, consider the following statements:
s: It requires adherence to constitutional ethos beyond mere legal compliance.
It privileges constitutional ethics over societal prejudice.
It is expressly defined in the Constitution.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The concept appears nowhere in the text — which is the basis of the ambiguity criticism.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (application of constitutional morality):
pairs: 1. Privacy as a fundamental right protecting autonomy and dignity
2. First invocation to strike down Section 377
3. Constitutional morality above popular sentiment on temple entry
4. Decriminalisation of adultery on grounds of gender equality
bank.e: Naz on Section 377, Sabarimala on temple entry, Joseph Shine on adultery, and Puttaswamy on privacy.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the key dimensions of constitutional morality?
o: Rule of law and equality before it
bank.e: The doctrine exists precisely to override prevailing social consensus where it conflicts with constitutional values.

bank.as: Constitutional morality is criticised as open-ended.
bank.rs: Its indeterminacy leaves room for judicial subjectivity and risks overreach.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the reason clearer articulation and consistent application head the reform proposals.

bank.q: Navtej Singh Johar (2018) overturned which decision?
bank.e: Koushal (2013), which had itself reversed Naz Foundation. Navtej restored and reinforced the constitutional morality reasoning.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the significance of the doctrine:
s: It reinforces India's commitment to transformative constitutionalism.
It prioritises constitutional ethics over majoritarian impulses.
It has been uniformly accepted in society wherever applied.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sabarimala demonstrates that societal and political resistance can follow a judgment grounded in the doctrine.

bank.q: All of the following are proposed to strengthen the doctrine EXCEPT:
o: Clear judicial articulation and consistent application
Subjecting its application to a popular referendum
bank.e: A referendum would subordinate constitutional morality to popular morality — the exact inversion the doctrine exists to prevent.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
bank.e: Naz Foundation (2009) → Koushal (2013) → Puttaswamy (2017) → Navtej Singh Johar (2018).

bank.q: Which of the following best captures the doctrine's function?
o: A compass guiding governance beyond transient societal prejudice
A limit on the jurisdiction of High Courts
bank.e: A compass transcending transient prejudice to uphold enduring constitutional values — its role in Naz, Navtej, Sabarimala and Puttaswamy alike.
